title: Writing a word and returning to the origin
statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $i$ be one of the $k$ work tapes, let $w_0$ be a finite word, and let $d$ be a configuration on an arbitrary fixed input whose state is the initial writing phase. After $2|w_0|+2$ steps, the machine that writes $w_0$ and returns its head to the origin is in its done state; on tape $i$, it has written $w_0$ starting at its initial head position, and all other cells and tapes retain their previous contents. At every time $t<2|w_0|+2$, its state is not the done state. For every time $t\le 2|w_0|+2$, the head on tape $i$ lies between its initial position and that position plus $|w_0|$, inclusive, and every other tape head remains at its initial position.
hypotheses_covered: $i$ is an index among the $k$ work tapes
$d$ is a configuration on a fixed input
The initial state of $d$ is the initial writing phase
